bandReport.notes: Band ends the paper. Q100 is present and complete on p20 (printed page 43) with all four options; the booklet still prints '[ P.T.O.' at the foot of p20, but the PDF has no page 21 and Q100 is the last item. Head seam: p16 (printed 35) carries Q85 and Q86, both self-contained 'Question + two Statements' items that begin and end on that page, so nothing straddles into p17. No Directions block opens before p17 that reaches into this band. Two Directions sets both START on p20 and are owned here in full: 'For the following two (02) items :' over the athletic-children distance table (Q97, Q98, left column) and 'For the following two (02) items :' over the median-24 marks distribution (Q99, Q100, right column). No printed figures anywhere in this band — Q87 to Q90 are data-sufficiency items whose geometry is described entirely in words, and Q91 to Q100 are statistics items whose only visual matter is three ruled data tables (Q93 stem, Q97-98 context, Q99-100 context), all transcribed as GFM pipe tables. Q87 to Q90 continue the data-sufficiency block that runs from p16; each is a complete self-contained item with the same four fixed options. All numeric values, table cells and option texts on all four pages were re-checked against 5x-6x crops of the source PDF.

questions.stem:
A Question is given followed by two Statements I and II. Consider the Question and the Statements.

Question :

AB and CD are chords of a circle intersecting at P. If \(AP \times PB = 48\) square units, then what is \(CP \times PD\) equal to?

Statement-I :

\(AP = 8\) units

Statement-II :

\(CP = 10\) units

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Question and the Statements?

options.label: A
options.text: The Question can be answered by using one of the Statements alone, but cannot be answered using the other Statement alone

options.label: B
options.text: The Question can be answered by using either Statement alone

options.label: C
options.text: The Question can be answered by using both the Statements together, but cannot be answered using either Statement alone

options.label: D
options.text: The Question can be answered even without using any of the Statements

questions.subtopic: Intersecting Chords and Power of a Point
flags: Invented subtopic. The intersecting-chords product relation (AP.PB = CP.PD) has no home among the catalog's four Circles subtopics (Chords and Perpendiculars / Tangents and Secants / Angles in a Circle / Two Circles and Common Tangents); 'Chords and Perpendiculars' is about the perpendicular-from-centre results, which is a different theorem.

questions.stem:
The frequency distribution of marks of 100 candidates in a particular examination is as follows :

| Marks | Number of Candidates |
|---|---|
| More than 10 | 100 |
| More than 20 | 75 |
| More than 30 | 60 |
| More than 40 | 40 |

What are the average marks of the candidates?
flags: Transcribed as printed. The table is a 'more than' cumulative distribution whose last row is 'More than 40 = 40'; the booklet states no upper class limit for that final class. Verified against a 5x crop of the source page - only four rows are printed and there is no fifth row or footnote.
